renal_basis.note: Less than 1% of esomeprazole is excreted unchanged in urine; pharmacokinetics are not expected to be altered in renal impairment.

hepatic.value: No dosage adjustment necessary in mild to moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Classes A and B). In severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C), AUC is 2-3 times higher: maximum dosage 20 mg once daily (or starting dosage 20 mg twice daily for pathological hypersecretory conditions).

refs.quote: Dosage modification of esomeprazole magnesium delayed-release capsules is recommended for patients with severe hepatic impairment for the healing of EE, risk reduction of NSAID-associated gastric ulcer, H. pylori eradication to reduce the risk of duodenal ulcer recurrence, and pathological hypersecretory conditions including Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome
In patients with mild to moderate liver impairment (Child-Pugh Classes A and B), no dosage adjustment is necessary.

Esomeprazole belongs to a class of antisecretory compounds, the substituted benzimidazoles, that suppress gastric acid secretion by specific inhibition of the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of the gastric parietal cell.

mg_safety.note: Proton pump inhibitor; no neuromuscular junction blocking activity (monitor for hypomagnesemia with prolonged therapy).

value.instructions: Do NOT chew or crush capsules or granules. Open capsule and empty granules into a 60 mL catheter-tipped syringe with 50 mL water; shake vigorously for 15 seconds, administer immediately through the nasogastric tube, and flush with additional water. Do not administer if granules have dissolved or disintegrated.

refs.quote: Attach the catheter-tipped syringe to a nasogastric tube and deliver the contents of the syringe through the nasogastric tube into the stomach. After administering the granules, flush the nasogastric tube with additional water. Use the mixture immediately after preparation. Do not administer the granules if they have dissolved or disintegrated.

pgx.value: Metabolized predominantly by CYP2C19 (polymorphic: ~3% of Caucasians and 15-20% of Asians are CYP2C19 poor metabolizers). At steady state with 40 mg once daily, AUC ratio in poor vs extensive metabolizers is ~1.5, which is not considered clinically meaningful.

refs.quote: Approximately 3% of Caucasians and 15 to 20% of Asians are CYP2C19 poor metabolizers.

At steady state following once daily administration of esomeprazole 40 mg, the ratio of AUC in poor metabolizers to AUC in the rest of the population (EMs) is approximately 1.5. This change in exposure is not considered clinically meaningful.

mechanism_of_action.value: Substituted benzimidazole proton pump inhibitor (S-isomer of omeprazole) that is protonated in the acidic compartment of gastric parietal cells to form the active achiral sulphenamide inhibitor, specifically inhibiting the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme system ('acid pump') to block the final step of basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion.

refs.quote: Esomeprazole belongs to a class of antisecretory compounds, the substituted benzimidazoles, that suppress gastric acid secretion by specific inhibition of the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of the gastric parietal cell.
Esomeprazole is a time-dependent inhibitor of CYP2C19, resulting in autoinhibition and nonlinear pharmacokinetics.

The major part of esomeprazole’s metabolism is dependent upon the CYP2C19 isoenzyme, which forms the hydroxy and desmethyl metabolites. The remaining amount is dependent on CYP3A4 which forms the sulphone metabolite.

enzyme_profile.note: Major substrate and time-dependent inhibitor of CYP2C19; minor substrate of CYP3A4.

value.effect: Increased INR and prothrombin time in patients receiving PPIs and warfarin concomitantly, which may lead to abnormal bleeding and death.
value.management: Monitor INR and prothrombin time and adjust the dose of warfarin if needed to maintain the target INR range.

refs.quote: Warfarin Clinical Impact: Increased INR and prothrombin time in patients receiving PPIs, including esomeprazole, and warfarin concomitantly. Increases in INR and prothrombin time may lead to abnormal bleeding and even death.

value.effect: May elevate and prolong serum concentrations of methotrexate and/or hydroxymethotrexate, possibly leading to methotrexate toxicities.
value.management: A temporary withdrawal of esomeprazole may be considered in some patients receiving high-dose methotrexate.

refs.quote: Concomitant use of esomeprazole with methotrexate (primarily at high dose) may elevate and prolong serum concentrations of methotrexate and/or its metabolite hydroxymethotrexate, possibly leading to methotrexate toxicities.

value.effect: Potential for increased exposure of digoxin (omeprazole increased digoxin bioavailability by 10%, up to 30% in two subjects).
value.management: Monitor digoxin concentrations and adjust the dose if needed to maintain therapeutic drug concentrations.

tier.note: No adequate well-controlled studies with esomeprazole in pregnant women, though large epidemiologic studies with omeprazole (S/R-isomer; e.g., 1,800 Danish first-trimester exposures showing 2.9% vs 2.6% birth defects; 955 Swedish registry infants) did not demonstrate increased overall major congenital malformations. Animal studies showed no teratogenicity with esomeprazole, though pre/postnatal rat bone changes occurred when dosed through lactation.

refs.quote: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies with esomeprazole in pregnant women. Esomeprazole is the S-isomer of omeprazole.
